key_insight: A2M shows that MCP agents can be hijacked without internal access by exploiting how they semantically choose tools and trust tool outputs. It combines prompt/metadata attraction with trace-guided manipulation to steer agent behavior toward attacker goals.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the semantic supply-chain risk in Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystems, where third-party tool metadata and returned outputs can be attacker-controlled. This creates a black-box path for influencing which tools agents invoke and how they act after invocation.
method: Attraction phase: optimize tool metadata so an MCP agent is more likely to select the attacker’s tool during semantic matching.
Manipulation phase: use execution traces to iteratively refine malicious tool outputs so they better steer the agent’s next actions.
Black-box design: requires no internal model access, relying only on observable agent behavior and tool interaction patterns.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights a practical attack surface in agentic systems that connect to third-party tools. It underscores the need for stronger tool vetting, output sanitization, and security monitoring in MCP-based deployments.

paper_title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
paper_authors: Laizhen Li, Xuan Wang, Peicheng Zhao, Juanjuan Zhao, Kejiang Ye
